newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end softer as electronics slide.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end softer as electronics slide.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly lower on Friday on profit-taking in the electronics sector, but brokers said they expected prices to firm.
The index ended down 14.73 points or 0.23 percent at 6,290.23. Turnover was a modest T$31.22 billion.

Profit-takers erased some recent gains in electronics shares but the damage was limited. "Most electronics closed above their lows, indicating the correction is over. They should rise again to lead the overall upward momentum," said Alex Chiu of Capital Securities. Acer dipped to T$39 but ended at T$39.3, down 60 cents. Macronix hit T$35.2 but closed at T$35.6, down 20 cents.
Cement and steel shares also fell.
Taiwan Styrene and Grand Petrochemical rose 60 cents and 40 cents to T$36.1 and T$27.1, respectively, on expected price hikes for petrochemical material styrene monomer, brokers said.
Paper shares rose on expected product price hikes.
Some brokers attributed the index fall in part to caution over Wall Street's overnight fall and the Iraq military conflict.
But brokers said they saw a firming trend ahead, with electronics shares likely to lead the way.
"Most electronics still enjoyed profit growth in the first half of this year, although the growth was slower than expected due to an industry oversupply," Chiu said.
"With most expecting electronics to have sound performance in the third and fourth quarters, their hot-sale season, the sector should rise to trigger an overall firming trend."
Fuelling sentiment for an upturn were hopes that the government would take more measures to boost economic growth, which is lagging behind official forecasts, Chiu said.
For Saturday, a 6,300-6,370 range was seen.
